h1: The 6 Best Cordless Vacuums Under $200 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Cordless Vacuums Under $200: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six cordless stick vacuums that all sit under $200, ranked by listed battery run time and power for apartments and homes.
summary: The Uosogi is the best cordless vacuum under $200 on paper, listing 70 minutes of run time and 650W. The JELLYPIG lists identical figures and sits just behind it. The Levoit and Electrolux offer 50 minutes from known brands, the Hoover lists 45, and the Shark Pet is the short-run option at 40 minutes.
intro: Run time is the number that decides whether a cordless vacuum retires your corded one or becomes another gadget you charge between rooms. In this price range the listed minutes nearly double from the bottom of the ranking to the top, and that gap says more about daily use than any brand badge on the handle. A 40 minute battery cleans a studio. A 70 minute battery cleans a house.

All six vacuums here sit in the $100 to $200 bracket. We ranked them on listed run time and power rating, and the listings say little else, so we state where a spec is missing. Listed minutes usually describe the lowest suction mode, which means real runs at full power will be shorter, so treat the minutes as a ceiling, not a promise.

products.name: Uosogi Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: The longest listed run time here, 70 minutes, with 650W.
products.description:
The Uosogi lists a 70 minute run time and a 650W motor rating in a cordless design, in the $100 to $200 bracket. Seventy minutes is the number to remember. It is long enough for a multi-room home in one session, which is the difference between a vacuum you grab daily and one that sits on its dock. The 650W figure is the highest wattage here, although wattage only loosely tracks suction.

It leads because no other vacuum in this bracket lists more minutes, and it pairs them with the top wattage. The trade against name brands is that the listing is thin beyond those two numbers.

Buy it for a larger apartment or house where you clean several rooms in one go. Check what attachments are in the box, and weigh the lesser-known brand against the extra minutes.
products.idealFor: Larger homes needing long run time.

products.name: JELLYPIG Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: Matches the 70 minute and 650W figures of the top pick.
products.description:
The JELLYPIG lists the same 70 minute run time and 650W rating as the Uosogi, in the $100 to $200 bracket. On paper the two are twins, and either one beats the shorter-running vacuums below by 20 minutes or more.

It sits second only because there is nothing to separate the two on specs, and the Uosogi takes the tiebreak. For a shopper, that means price should decide: if the JELLYPIG is cheaper on the day you buy, it is the better choice. Little brand history stands behind it, and the listing reveals little beyond the two numbers.

It works for anyone who sees it at a lower price than the Uosogi. Skip it if you want detailed specs, attachments or a well-known name. Compare warranty terms, because a long battery that fails early is no bargain.
products.idealFor: Shoppers comparing it against the Uosogi on price.

products.name: Levoit Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: A named brand with a listed 50 minute run time.
products.description:
The Levoit lists a 50 minute run time on a cordless body, in the $100 to $200 bracket. Wattage is not given, so suction cannot be compared with the 650W pair. A recognized brand name matters here for support and parts, which the lesser-known leaders cannot match.

It places third because it gives up 20 minutes to the 70-minute pair, partly offset by the better-known maker. It is level with the Electrolux on run time. For a one or two bedroom home, 50 minutes is enough to cover the floors in a single session.

It suits smaller homes. Skip it if you need more than 50 minutes, or if you want a stated wattage. Compare suction by reading owner feedback, since the listing gives no figure, and check which attachments are included.

products.name: Electrolux WellQ7 Cordless 2-in-1 Vacuum with High Suction Power and
products.description:
The Electrolux WellQ7 is a cordless 2-in-1 vacuum with a listed 50 minute run time, in the $100 to $200 bracket. A 2-in-1 design splits into a handheld, which is useful for stairs, upholstery and the inside of a car, where a full stick is awkward.

It ties the Levoit on minutes and ranks below it only because the Levoit's listing is simpler. The 2-in-1 design is the difference that matters: if you clean sofas, steps or pet beds, the handheld mode is worth more than a spec you cannot verify. The listing title is truncated, and no wattage appears.

It is for buyers who want a handheld option as well. Confirm in the full listing how the conversion works, and check the weight, because a 2-in-1 can feel heavier than a plain stick.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting a handheld as well.

products.name: Hoover ONEPWR WindTunnel Emerge Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: A ONEPWR stick vacuum with a listed 45 minutes.
products.description:
The Hoover ONEPWR WindTunnel Emerge is a cordless stick vacuum with a listed 45 minute run time, in the $100 to $200 bracket. The ONEPWR name hints at a shared battery system across Hoover tools, though the listing does not spell it out.

It ranks fifth for giving up 5 minutes to the Levoit and Electrolux, and no wattage is listed. If you already own ONEPWR tools, the battery-sharing angle could be the reason to choose it. If you do not, it offers a little less than the competition at the same bracket.

It suits Hoover loyalists. Skip it if you want the longest run time. Verify battery sharing in the full listing, and check whether the battery is included, because ONEPWR listings do not always include the pack.
products.skipIf: You want the longest run time.

products.name: Shark Pet Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: A name-brand pet stick vacuum with 40 minutes listed.
products.description:
The Shark Pet is a cordless stick vacuum with a listed 40 minute run time, in the $100 to $200 bracket. The Shark name has a large following, and the pet focus suggests attention to hair and dander, though the listing gives no detail on how.

It ranks last because 40 minutes is the shortest run time in this ranking, 30 minutes behind the Uosogi. No wattage is stated either, which leaves you relying on brand reputation. For a small apartment, that is workable. For a big house, you would finish with a flat battery.

It works for small spaces and quick cleanups. Skip it if you clean a large home in one go. If your floor area is more than a couple of rooms, the longer-running Levoit or Uosogi will save you a recharge.
products.skipIf: You clean a large home in one go.

whatMatters.detail: Run time is how many minutes the battery lasts, usually at the lowest power mode. A short run time means stopping mid-clean. Find the minutes figure in the title or bullets and match it to your home size. Expect less at full power and plan for a second charge in a larger home.

Watts describe motor input, which loosely relates to suction. A higher number can mean stronger pickup, but it is not a full measure. Look for it in the listing, and note when it is missing. The Uosogi and JELLYPIG list 650W, while the other four omit it, so suction comparisons are guesswork, and owner feedback becomes your best guide.

A 2-in-1 splits into a handheld for stairs, upholstery and car interiors. It is more versatile but may be heavier. A plain stick is lighter and quicker to grab. Check how the conversion works in the listing, as on the Electrolux WellQ7, and whether the handheld includes attachments, such as a crevice tool or brush.

Some brands share batteries across tools, which lowers cost if you own other tools from that line. The Hoover ONEPWR name hints at this. Check whether the battery is included, and whether the listing says the pack fits other tools you own, because shared packs save real money and reduce clutter in the charging corner.

Several listings omit wattage or attachments, and you cannot compare what is missing. Read the full listing and the questions section before you buy. A gap in a product page is either a feature the maker prefers not to advertise or a detail the seller never filled in, and you should find out which before paying.

faq.q: Does the listed run time match real use?
faq.a: Listed run time is usually for the lowest setting, so expect less at full power. The 70 minutes on the Uosogi will shrink sharply when you use maximum suction on carpet, so plan on fewer rooms per charge.

Buying on brand without checking minutes. In this bracket the range is 40 to 70, so a Shark Pet runs 30 minutes less than the Uosogi. Match minutes to your floor area, and count the rooms you clean in one pass.

faq.q: Is the Uosogi worth it over Shark?
faq.a: On paper yes for run time, with 70 minutes against 40. The Shark has a stronger brand and a pet focus, though, so choose based on home size and how much you trust the Uosogi's maker.

Dock or plug per the manual. Charge fully before first use, and keep the battery away from heat. Charging times are not given in the listings here, so check the manual, and do not leave it on the dock unattended overnight.

faq.q: How do I maintain a cordless vacuum?
faq.a: Empty the bin and clean the filter regularly. A clogged filter cuts suction and shortens run time, which is the spec you paid for with the Uosogi or JELLYPIG, so make it a monthly habit.

faq.q: Do all of these cost under $200?
faq.a: All sit in the $100 to $200 bucket in our data, but check the live price. Sales can push any of them above or below the bracket, so compare the day you buy and read the return window.

finalTake: Buy the Uosogi, or the JELLYPIG if it is cheaper, when you want the longest listed run time. Choose the Levoit for a smaller home from a known brand, the Electrolux if a 2-in-1 handheld matters, and the Shark Pet for quick pet cleanups. Match minutes to your floor area before you weigh brand.
